description: Subscription plan changes (POST /subscriptions/businesses/:businessId/trial, /activate, /cancel, /checkout, /record-payment) are OWNER only: the OWNER membership or Business.ownerId (the rule IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner applies, owner ruling D-11) and SUPER_ADMIN (the BusinessGuard platform bypass); every other member gets 403 {code:'SUBSCRIPTION_OWNER_ONLY'} with no Subscription, SubscriptionPayment or audit row written; each successful change writes one team_activity_logs row (module billing) naming the acting user, in the same transaction; read routes keep the membership rule. Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/subscriptions-authority.integration.test.ts src/modules/subscriptions/subscriptions.controller.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-08c-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/subscriptions-authority.json --report .proof/r0-08c-vitest.json. Cases tagged RED-BEFORE fail on the unmodified code (the R0 working branch at 8b8cf715; the tests-first commit 183110f9 records the tally: R01 STAFF with every scope none record-payment KEYFLOW -> 201 ACTIVE, R02 cancel -> 201). The web half (billing-tab shows "Only the business owner can change the plan." on SUBSCRIPTION_OWNER_ONLY) is apps/web/src/app/app/settings/business/__tests__/billing-tab-owner-only.test.tsx.
notes: OPEN POLICY QUESTION D-33 (recorded, not decided): an owner's self-declared manual payment (POST /record-payment) still activates a paid plan and records a COMPLETED SubscriptionPayment with no money moving, and POST /activate does the same for any gateway string with no payment at all. Whether manual recording should instead create a PENDING payment that platform staff confirm is a new owner decision. Case R0-08c-O04 pins today's answer so a change is deliberate.

Read routes (current, billing-dashboard, history, check-limit, payments) keep the BusinessGuard membership rule: no billing module scope exists in core/authority/module-vocabulary.ts, and none of these routes carries a RequireModuleScope today, so nothing was tightened (cases G01, G02, U09).
checkout writes no Subscription row; it is still owner-only and writes one audit row (subscription_checkout_started) so the start of a paid plan change names its actor.

Review finding ST-R008c-1 (repair): plan changes were atomic but not serialized, so concurrent owner record-payments or activates each added an ACTIVE row (the review probe: 4 parallel record-payments left 4 ACTIVE subscriptions, every audit row saying replacedSubscriptions:1, and after a 201 cancel GET /current still reported KEYFLOW ACTIVE), and concurrent trial starts passed a check made outside the transaction. Every plan change now runs in one transaction whose first statement is pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('subscriptions:plan-change:' || businessId)); the trial check runs under it; activations and cancel cancel every ACTIVE/TRIALING row and record the ids (replacedSubscriptionIds, cancelledSubscriptionIds) on the audit row. Cases K01-K04 (real database, parallel requests) and U10-U11 (pure) prove it; K01-K04 and U10 fail on the pre-repair service.
